_readme: Every variable this chain needs from OUTSIDE itself, and the source the owner's machine resolves it from. A parity run fills the values by running HIS resolve_source() over these source strings for the brand under test, then passes the result as --config. It is a template, not a config: it names no brand and holds no value (workspace rule 7), and it is never read by the engine.

avatars.means: a query against the brand's language bank

today.means: computed by his machine at run time

avatar.means: a workspace-relative file, read by his machine

identity_anchors.means: a workspace-relative file, read by his machine

language.means: a query against the brand's language bank

language_bank.means: a workspace-relative file, read by his machine

offer_file.means: a workspace-relative file, read by his machine

product_file.means: a workspace-relative file, read by his machine

production_route.means: a fixed value in his chain config

objection_bank.means: a workspace-relative file, read by his machine

creator_profile.damon_source: =UNASSIGNED. The run supplies this when it is a creator's own post. Never name a creator here.
creator_profile.means: a fixed value in his chain config

source_url.means: supplied by the run (gathered by his machine)

video.means: supplied by the run as a LOCATION (a path or a URI); his machine takes it as a call ARGUMENT, not a prompt token, and neither engine opens it to pipe it

product_images.means: supplied by the run as a LOCATION (a path or a URI); his machine takes it as a call ARGUMENT, not a prompt token, and neither engine opens it to pipe it

product_look.means: a workspace-relative file, read by his machine

creator_record.means: supplied by the run (gathered by his machine)

existing_profile.means: supplied by the run (gathered by his machine)

handle.means: supplied by the run (gathered by his machine)

profile_spec.means: supplied by the run (gathered by his machine)

teardown_material.means: supplied by the run (gathered by his machine)
